hooks.command: echo "{\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"hookEventName\":\"UserPromptSubmit\",\"additionalContext\":\"PLAIN ENGLISH RULE (from CLAUDE.md): Alex is not a native English speaker. Write the SHORTEST version he still understands - not fewer words, not more. If he has to ask what it means it was too short; twelve comment lines over sixteen code lines is too long. A fragment is fine when it is clear alone, so do not pad a line into a sentence. Use common words. No metaphors, no idioms, no clever phrasing. Avoid words like load-bearing, the other way round, common thread, greppable, breaks quietly, worth your attention. Give the short answer first, then the reason. Use a plain list instead of a table when the cells hold sentences.\"},\"suppressOutput\":true}"

statusLine.command: input=$(cat); model=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.model.display_name'); ctx=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.context_window.used_percentage // empty'); five=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage // empty'); week=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage // empty'); effort=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.effort.level // empty'); out="$model"; [ -n "$effort" ] && out="$out ($effort)"; [ -n "$ctx" ] && out="$out | Context: $(printf '%.0f' "$ctx")%"; [ -n "$five" ] && out="$out | 5h: $(printf '%.0f' "$five")%"; [ -n "$week" ] && out="$out | 7d: $(printf '%.0f' "$week")%"; echo "$out"
